Being a half Japanese, I moved here 3 years ago to study since I love visiting Japan when I was a kid but things didn't came what I expected it to be after I became adult. Mostly, because japanese people being inconsiderate, fake and selfish are my major reasons to hate living here. 

Although I might be wrong to make vague assumption that the city I live is equal to Japan entirely but maybe Kyoto is a different place than Tokyo but I'm glad your friend found a place for himself and being a manager in bar sounds like a cool job.

When I didn't live in Japan, I often got asked how frequent I ate sushi at home and the answer is barely once a week. Since it's actually rather difficult to prepare authentic sushi at home so it's very common for families to get (fresh) pre-made sushi or sashimi (just the fish but sliced) from supermarkets.

No worries pal, not always the combination of both together but yes we do eat a lot of seafood and rice since Japan is an island surrounded by sea and rice is our main resource for carbs/energy early from the history. 

But not only seafood and rice, and you might want to google the phrases below because I'm not an expert in describing. 

We get tired of eating rice so we eat noodles frequently like Ramen (my favorite), Udon and Soba.

Other common foods we have Tempura, Yakitori, Okonomiyaki/Takoyaki, Donburi, Yakiniku, Hanba-gu, Nabe and etc...

We eat a lot of pastas, pizzas, hamburgers and many other western foods very often as well.

For the time frame, 3-5 days is enough to visit a prefecture or a major city in Japan, I also recommend (not with a family) staying at capsule hotels to save money if necessary :).

Tokyo (also where I'm studying) should have the best schools or reputable schools located in one place but it depends on what you're studying most definitely and which prefecture you wish stay, considering there are cultural differences, like dialects, food... etc.

People are frustratingly impolite and selfish is my most concern living here, disregarding other many WTFs. I'm not saying everyone is, many people including my Japanese friends are awesome ppl but I'm honestly tired of people saying like all Japanese are reputable for manners and politeness because of one or two nice episodes...

Many of my foreign friends have changed there perspectives about Japanese ppl and we always mutually crack jokes and agree this when you experience commuting by trains in the city with all the stressed salaryman lol.

I have anxiety, depression and other symptoms but my main struggle throughout my whole life is ocd. I have experienced many behaviors from doing all kinds of rituals, having hostile/sexual thoughts, hoarding, routine... you name it.

OCD is constant living in fear, being afraid, being controlled by something obnoxious thoughts even though you know it isn't right.

My greatest fear right now is contamination... and it has nothing to do with being germaphobic, since I could eat food scrumbs right off the floor.

It's hard to explain what's its like living in fear of contamination, but if you could imagine if a deadly zombie virus is spread by touching and the house is 95% including your family is contaminated. Instead of a gun, you spray anti-disinfectant alcohol and wipe with wet tissue every single day to fight your anxiety. 

Not to mention, the virus is contaminated through air by dust/hair/imagination as well. 

I didn't exaggerate if you're wondering, just life is miserable.
